text:
Kyra: Quick heads-up — after the merge to release/2026-03-16 we're seeing CI perf/regressions and OOMs on the long-context perf suite. Canaries started failing around the same time. PR/commit that landed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/commit/abcdef. Rolling back that merge on one canary stopped the OOMs. Need a quick triage and hold if it's a rollout blocker.

Devin: I reproduced locally. longctx-suite spikes memory use after ~3k tokens and then OOMs. Artifact from CI has heap snapshots and perf flamegraphs: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/1989991234. Looks like KV cache fragment count climbs steadily.

perf-bot: [automated] perf-ci: longctx-suite failed on node gpu-x1 — OOM at 00:12:34. Heap snapshot: /artifacts/1989991234/heap.html; flamegraph: /artifacts/1989991234/flame.svg

Anna: Can we bisect the merge range? I suspect kernel-routing heuristics commit, it changed kernel selection thresholds for >256 seq to prefer torch-kernel-v2 which also changes allocator slab sizing. I can run bisect if folks agree.

Simon: Observed behaviour in logs: repeated large slab allocs with tiny frees -> fragmentation. My hunch: kernel selection change routes longctx workloads to a path that uses 1MB mmap slabs and smaller frees, causing fragmentation under many concurrent streams. Candidate commits to check: 0xabc123 (kernel-router rewrite), 0xdef456 (batching heuristic tweak).

Kyra: Paste of the relevant runtime snippet from a failing canary: 
```
runtime: slab alloc 1mb from mmap
runtime: slab free 256kb
runtime: kv_cache: fragment_count=3248, free_buckets=12
OOM: alloc failed for kv_page 4096
```

Devin: Reproducer command I used: `./tests/run_longctx_local --seq-len 4096 --streams 16 --iters 1000`. On my devbox, flipping `KERNEL_ROUTER=legacy` removes the spike entirely.

Anna: Starting bisect (range a1b2..f3e4) with kernel-router toggles. I'll run on the same CI amber node config and post results.

perf-bot: bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood/bisect/1989991234. Expected ~6 runs.

Simon: If bisect points to 0xabc123 we should consider an immediate rollback or pinning kernel selection in canary. Also short-term mitigation: increase kv cache compaction frequency and lower slab size for mmap path. Longer-term: add seqlen-tail perf test to CI.

Kyra: Hold rollout for that release until we confirm. If bisect confirms kernel-router commit, we'll either revert or pin canary to legacy selection. @oncall-bot please pause ongoing deploys for the release channel.

oncall-bot: Deployment pause requested for cluster 'prod-gpu' by Kyra. Confirm pause? :warning:

Devin: Pushed a quick canary pin patch to test legacy kernel for seqlen>1024: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/pull/4320 — running CI now.

Anna: Bisect finished: culprit identified as commit 0xabc123 (kernel-router heuristic rewrite). Bisect log: https://ci.redwood/bisect/1989991234/result.txt. I started a revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/pull/4321 (draft). Local CI on revert branch is green on longctx-suite.

Simon: Please add a perf regression test that simulates seqlen tail (multi-stream longctx workload). I'll draft a test harness. Also add a check in CI to run the KV cache fragment counter and fail on sustained growth.

Kyra: Thanks all. Action items: Anna finish revert PR + get approval, Devin monitor pinned canary, Simon add regression test, ops keep rollout paused until revert lands or we have a safer mitigation. Keep updates short in this thread. :thumbsup:
